newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's CANTV agrees 118 pct pay rise -- paper. [CORRECTED 1:10 GMT 11/6]
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's CANTV agrees 118 pct pay rise -- paper. [CORRECTED 1:10 GMT 11/6]

text.p: (Corrects to remove reference to rise being retroactive).
Venezuela's privatised telephone company CANTV has agreed to a pay rise of 118 percent for its workers, according to a local press report on Tuesday.
The agreement was signed by CANTV and its workers on Monday after two months of arbitration, and CANTV estimates it will cost the company about 179.6 billion bolivars ($374 million), the report said.

The payment would be paid in two phases, with 60 percent paid when the findings are published in the official gazette and the remaining 40 percent one year later. It would be retroactive to January 1 this year.
Carlos Sainz Munoz, a representative of the CANTV workers, was reported as saying that employees would also receive a bonus payment of 60,000 bolivars ($125), and annual leave was set at 45 days.
Overtime and night-shift pay was raised by five percent, the report said.
CANTV and the workers also agreed to bonus and productivity payments no less than 20 percent of total salary, and a monthly family bonus of 50,000 bolivars ($104).
The company managed to reduce the number of holidays from 11 to five, the report said.
